system:
You are the test planner of a network change-validation pipeline. Given the change ticket, the
intent analysis and the configuration diff, write a change-specific test plan that (a) checks every effect the ticket
promises and (b) checks that nothing else that the diff could affect has changed (use expect "unchanged").
Also consider emulation-only risks: MTU (mtu probes), failover timers (conv), link load after path changes (load).
Typed test language (JSON objects; use ONLY these types and only names that exist):
  {"t":"reach","src":HOST,"dst":HOST|ROUTER,"svc":SVC|"*","expect":"allow"|"deny"|"unchanged"}
  {"t":"path","src":HOST,"dst":HOST,"via":ROUTER,"expect":true|false}
  {"t":"route","dev":ROUTER,"prefix":"a.b.c.d/n","expect":"present"|"absent"|"unchanged"}
  {"t":"adj","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"expect":"up"|"down"|"unchanged"}          (OSPF adjacency on a link)
  {"t":"mtu","src":HOST,"dst":HOST,"size":1500|9000,"expect":"pass"|"fail"}  (DF probe, emulation tier)
  {"t":"conv","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"max_s":3}                               (failover time of a link, emulation)
  {"t":"load","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"max_pct":90}                            (link utilisation, emulation)
  {"t":"like","host":HOST,"as":HOST}     (after a VLAN move / re-addressing: host has exactly the same access as the
                                          reference host, towards and from every other host and service)
SVC is one of: icmp, tcp/22, tcp/25, tcp/80, tcp/443, tcp/5432, udp/53.
Reply with JSON only: {"tests": [ ... ]}

CHANGE TICKET:
Stop announcing customer 2 to peer2.

INTENT ANALYSIS:
{"ticket_says": "Stop advertising customer 2's prefixes to peer2.", "goal": "Withdraw customer 2's route announcements toward peer2 while leaving other announcements unchanged.", "change_type": "bgp_policy", "scope": ["customer 2", "peer2"], "expected_effects": ["Customer 2's prefixes are no longer announced to peer2", "Peer2 no longer learns routes for customer 2"], "must_not_change": [], "confidence": "medium"}

CONFIG DIFF:
PAO | ip prefix-list PL_CUST_ALL | + ip prefix-list PL_CUST_ALL seq 3 deny 172.16.0.0/16 le 24

TOPOLOGY (2-hop around changed devices): devices ['AAR', 'BOU', 'CHM', 'HOU', 'PAO', 'SDG', 'SEA', 'SLC', 'cust1', 'peer2']; hosts ['ext-dns2']; links ['SEA--PAO (10000 Mbps)', 'SEA--SDG (10000 Mbps)', 'SEA--CHM (10000 Mbps)', 'PAO--SDG (10000 Mbps)', 'PAO--SLC (10000 Mbps)', 'SDG--HOU (10000 Mbps)', 'SLC--BOU (10000 Mbps)', 'SLC--AAR (2500 Mbps)', 'BOU--HOU (2500 Mbps)', 'SEA--cust1 (10000 Mbps)', 'PAO--peer2 (10000 Mbps)']
Hosts: c1-host(172.16.1.10,cust1,mtu 1500), c2-host(172.16.2.10,cust2,mtu 1500), c3-host(172.16.3.10,cust3,mtu 1500), ext-dns1(8.8.8.10,internet,mtu 1500), ext-dns2(1.1.1.10,internet,mtu 1500), noc1(10.99.0.10,noc,mtu 1500), noc2(10.99.0.11,noc,mtu 1500), noclab1(10.98.0.10,noc-lab,mtu 1500), noclab2(10.98.0.11,noc-lab,mtu 1500)
Routers: SEA, PAO, SDG, SLC, BOU, HOU, LNK, CHM, PIT, ATL, AAR, ITH, PRN, CPK, cust1, cust2, cust3, peer1, peer2
Network invariants (always checked): no forwarding loops; management host noc1 reaches every managed router; isolation pairs must stay blocked: [['c1-host', 'noc1'], ['ext-dns1', 'noc1'], ['c3-host', 'noc1'], ['ext-dns2', 'noclab1']]; external peers ['peer1', 'peer2', 'cust1', 'cust2', 'cust3'] must not learn ['10.0.0.0/8']; SLAs: failover <= 3.0 s, link utilisation <= 90.0%.
text:
The diff adds a deny for 172.16.0.0/16 le 24 to PL_CUST_ALL on PAO. The ticket's intent is to stop announcing customer 2 (172.16.2.0/24) to peer2. Note the deny covers all of 172.16.0.0/16 le 24, which also includes customer 1 (172.16.1.0/24) and customer 3 (172.16.3.0/24). That is likely over-broad, so the plan checks customer 2 withdrawal and also tests that other customers' announcements and reachability are unchanged. Since the prefix-list sits on PAO toward peer2, the tests probe route presence on peer2 and data-plane reachability.
